**Search process:**
- Declared three stopping rules upfront (best_so_far_above, failures_at_least, last_gain_at_most) and a prior favoring feature 0 (momentum-style) for non-data reasons.
- `init` anchored on feature 32 (Sharpe 0.385), not my prior — the data didn't support it.
- Extended and restarted across 7 different anchor features (32, 33, 18, 16, 19, 38, 14). Feature 35 (short) repeatedly emerged as the best complementary pairing across multiple anchors.
- The combination **[33+, 35-]** reached Sharpe 0.491 (all years equal) / 0.554 (recent years weighted) and was never beaten across 6 subsequent independent restarts — strong evidence of a genuine, robust local optimum rather than a lucky single draw.
- Adjusted triggers twice, transparently and with logged reasons, when the original parameters (calibrated without knowledge of this data's Sharpe range) proved miscalibrated — all changes were recorded as required.
- Confirmed the baseline model (Sharpe 0.183/0.246, turnover 0.042) was clearly dominated by the rule.

**Candidate submitted:** rule **[33+, 35-]** (long feature 33, short feature 35), equal-weighted.

**Prediction:** mean annualized net Sharpe **0.30**, sd **0.25** out-of-sample — a substantial haircut (~55-65% retention) from the in-sample 0.49 to account for search/selection bias and typical out-of-sample decay, while still reflecting the rule's robustness across multiple independent search branches.
